newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Kok to press Major on Europe before UK election.
newsitem.headline: Kok to press Major on Europe before UK election.

text.p: The Netherlands, which holds the European Union presidency, said on Tuesday it would press ahead with key EU treaty reform talks with Britain even though a general election there could lead to a change of government.

British Prime Minister John Major's ruling Conservative Party, in power for over 17 years, must go to the polls by May 22, only weeks before the June Amsterdam summit which is scheduled to agree landmark EU reforms ahead of the 15-member bloc's planned enlargement.
"I want to re-emphasise that we wish to negotiate in a very serious and concrete way with Britain," Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok told a news conference.
"We are not just sitting back and waiting for what will happen after the (British) elections. We cannot afford the luxury of losing time."
Kok declined to speculate on the outcome of a working dinner with Major in The Hague later on Tuesday.
"We all know that the upcoming British election will have some influence on the IGC (inter-governmental conference treaty review) talks," he said.
"I am confident we will be able to make progress. Problems are there to be transformed into opportunities.
Major has come under pressure from those in his party opposed to closer European integration to distance Britain from Brussels or even leave the bloc altogether.

Asked whether a British election in May would leave enough time to seal an Amsterdam Treaty in June, Kok said: "If we only have six weeks then time would be limited. This is an extra impetus to make progress now."

But Kok, finance minister during the previous Dutch presidency which brokered the EU's Maastricht Treaty in 1991, recalled that, then, "real progress was only made in the last few weeks or, perhaps, only in the last few days".
